function: Learned joint beamforming and RIS phase-shift control (satellite and BS beamformers, RIS phases) that minimizes BS transmit power under communication and sensing SINR constraints (pp. 6-7).
system: GEO satellite ISAC, 4 Tx/Rx antennas, 4 single-antenna users; terrestrial ISAC BS 4 Tx/Rx antennas, 4 users, passive reflecting RIS N=64; 28 GHz Ka-band, 500 MHz (pp. 3, 9-10).
method: Federated multi-agent deep reinforcement learning: F-DDPG actor-critic, two hidden layers of 256 neurons, satellite and BS agents aggregated periodically at a gateway server; F-DQN variant (pp. 6-10).
data_channel: Own simulator, no dataset: satellite channel with free-space loss, beam pattern and log-normal rain fading; terrestrial LoS channel, -103.6 dB path loss; 100 realizations (pp. 4, 10).
test_conditions: Trained 2000-5000 episodes on one simulated setting; averages over 100 realizations; sweeps of power, SINR, N, M, K, CSI error; no stated unseen scenario (pp. 10-12).
baselines: Learned: F-DQN, conventional DDPG and DQN, centralized C-DDPG. Non-learned: exhaustive search, random RIS phases, no RIS, communication-only without sensing (pp. 10-11).
metrics: Minimum BS transmit power (dBm) and percent power reduction, convergence over episodes, beampattern gain of targets, versus SINR thresholds, RIS size, antennas, users, CSI error (pp. 10-13).
complexity: Asymptotic order O(E*T*Ct) for F-DDPG from actor and critic layer widths, and a layer-width sum for DQN; no FLOPs or runtime figures (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 4: "free space loss, the radiation pattern of the antenna, and rain attenuation" (custom satellite channel after [42]); p. 10: "we model the transmission path using a LoS approach". No 3GPP channel model, dataset or measurement is used.
q2_support: p. 10: "The numerical results presented are the average outcomes from 100 distinct channel realizations." Sweeps of N, M, K, SINR and CSI error (pp. 11-12) are curves of the same setting; no model trained on one condition and tested on another is stated.
q3_support: p. 10: "the RIS adopts a random passive beamforming approach"; p. 11: "superior performance compared to F-DQN, traditional DDPG, and DQN methods" (BS transmit power, Figs. 2, 4-7).
q4_support: p. 9: "overarching computational complexity of the algorithm across all iterations" expressed as O(E T Ct), with the DQN order also given.
q5_support: p. 10: "average outcomes from 100 distinct channel realizations" of simulated channels. The paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 6 by the specificity order: the learned satellite and BS agents control beams and power in a GEO satellite ISAC link, so 6 wins over 5 and 3. Federated learning here is digital weight aggregation at a gateway (p. 8), not over the air, so not area 7. q3: conventional DQN (Figs. 2, 4) is a standard learning algorithm on the same problem; C-DDPG and F-DQN are variants of the method and were not counted; random RIS, no RIS and exhaustive search are non-learned (Figs. 2, 5-7). TR 38.811 is cited only as background (p. 1, ref. [7]), not for the channel. Table II was read from the page image (p. 9); training lengths differ (E=5000 on p. 9, 2000 episodes on p. 10).
